c.tagline: Java's cultural soul — palaces, batik, and ancient temples.

taxi.fareNote: Blue Bird runs reliable metered taxis; elsewhere agree a price first, or use Gojek/Grab for fixed app pricing. Becak and andong fares are always negotiated up front.

emergency.note: 112 is the general nationwide emergency line; 110 reaches police and 113 the fire service.

hood_desc: Yogyakarta's famous main artery — a nonstop parade of batik shops, street-food stalls, markets, and malls running down to Beringharjo market; the busiest, most central base, within walking distance of the Kraton.

A warren of narrow gang (alleys) just off Malioboro and beside Tugu train station, long the city's backpacker enclave with cheap guesthouses, warungs, and easy transport links; central but quieter than the main street.

Yogyakarta's bohemian 'international village' south of the Kraton, lined with cozy cafes, art galleries, boutique hotels, and a lively night market; a stylish, laid-back base popular with younger travelers and digital nomads.

The walled royal heart of the city around the Sultan's Palace (Kraton), Taman Sari water castle, and the northern Alun-Alun square; steeped in Javanese court culture and best for travelers who want to be among the historic sights.

A historic old town southeast of the centre, once the 16th-century capital of the Mataram Sultanate and still famous for its silversmiths, heritage houses, and old mosque; a quieter, atmospheric area for craft and history lovers.
lodging: The Phoenix Hotel Yogyakarta - Handwritten Collection

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water; tap water is not potable.

transit.hours: Trans Jogja BRT buses run roughly 5:30 AM to 9:30 PM; becak and andong (horse carts) work the tourist core all day. No metro, so Gojek/Grab fill the late-night gap.
transit.note: Yogyakarta's public-transport backbone is the Trans Jogja BRT bus network covering the city, plus the KA Bandara train link to the airport. For short hops in the tourist core, cycle-rickshaws (becak) and horse-drawn andong are traditional options, alongside Gojek/Grab.
transit.pay: Trans Jogja is a flat ~3,600 IDR fare paid by tap card or QRIS; becak and andong fares are negotiated in cash before the ride.

train: Intercity trains from Yogyakarta (Tugu) and Lempuyangan stations to Jakarta, Bandung, Surabaya, and Solo

transit.m: KA Bandara YIA airport train to Yogyakarta (Tugu) Station (~35-40 min)
DAMRI airport shuttle bus to the city (~60-90 min)
Metered taxi to city center (60-75 min)

tip.r: Not expected; some restaurants add a 5-10% service charge. Rounding up or leaving small change for good service is appreciated.

food.name: Gudeg
food.desc: Young jackfruit slow-simmered for hours in coconut milk and palm sugar, served with rice, boiled egg, crackling beef skin and fiery krecek.

places.name: Gudeg Yu Djum
places.note: The best-known name in town; dry-style gudeg eaten at breakfast, go early before it sells out.

places.name: Gudeg Pawon
places.note: Cult late-night kitchen where you queue in the doorway and are served straight from the wood-fired pans.

places.name: Gudeg sellers on Jalan Wijilan
places.note: A whole street of competing gudeg houses beside the kraton walls; easy to compare styles.

food.name: Sate klathak
food.desc: Young goat grilled on iron bicycle spokes and seasoned with little more than salt and pepper, served with a light goat curry broth and rice.

places.name: Sate Klathak Pak Pong
places.note: The most famous klathak house; expect queues at dinner, worth the ride out of the city.

places.name: Sate Klathak Pak Bari
places.note: Inside the old market building, the original klathak neighbourhood.

places.name: Sate Klathak Pak Jede
places.note: Later-opening alternative when Pak Pong is at its busiest.

food.name: Oseng mercon
food.desc: Literally firecracker stir-fry: beef fat, skin and tendon cooked down with a punishing amount of bird's eye chilli. Order rice and iced tea.

places.name: Oseng-Oseng Mercon Bu Narti
places.note: The original, open from evening onwards on the pavement; the dish that started the trend.

places.name: Warungs on Jalan KH Ahmad Dahlan
places.note: Several rival mercon stalls set up along the same stretch after dark.

places.name: Gudeg Mercon stalls
places.note: Chilli-heavy gudeg variants for anyone who wants the heat with jackfruit instead of beef.

food.name: Angkringan nasi kucing
food.desc: Cat rice - tiny banana-leaf parcels of rice with anchovy sambal or tempeh, eaten at pavement carts with skewers of gizzard, egg and tofu.

places.name: Angkringan Lik Man
places.note: The city's most famous angkringan, running late into the night; also the home of kopi joss.

places.name: Angkringan carts on Jalan Wongsodirjan
places.note: Row of tarpaulin-covered carts around the station, busiest after 9pm.

places.name: Angkringan at Alun-Alun Kidul
places.note: Snack carts ringing the southern palace square, good with the evening crowds.

food.name: Ayam goreng kampung
food.desc: Free-range chicken simmered in coconut water and spices, then deep fried until the crumbly kremes topping shatters; served with sambal and rice.

places.name: Ayam Goreng Ny Suharti
places.note: Yogyakarta institution and the name most associated with kremes-style fried chicken.

places.name: Ayam Goreng Mbok Berek
places.note: Long-established roadside kitchen on the Prambanan road, the original Kalasan style.

places.name: Gudeg Yu Djum
places.note: Serves it as the side to gudeg if you want both classics on one plate.

food.name: Bakpia pathok
food.desc: Small soft-baked pastries filled with sweetened mung bean paste, now also cheese, chocolate or durian - the standard edible souvenir from Jogja.

places.name: Bakpia Pathok 25
places.note: Best known of the Pathuk bakeries; buy them warm from the counter rather than boxed.

places.name: Bakpia Pathok 75
places.note: Rival long-running bakery a few streets away, with an open production room.

places.name: Bakpia Kurnia Sari
places.note: Softer, more modern style with fillings beyond mung bean.

food.name: Wedang ronde
food.desc: Hot ginger and lemongrass broth with chewy glutinous rice balls filled with peanut, plus bread cubes and peanuts - a cool-evening street drink.

places.name: Wedang Ronde Mbah Payem
places.note: Long-running ronde cart near the Great Mosque, a Yogyakarta night-time fixture.

places.name: Ronde carts at Alun-Alun Kidul
places.note: Set up around the south square each evening; also do wedang bajigur and jahe.

places.name: Carts along Malioboro
places.note: Easy first taste while walking the main street after dark.

food.name: Kopi joss
food.desc: Sweet black coffee with a lump of glowing charcoal dropped straight into the glass - it fizzes, softens the acidity and is pure Jogja theatre.

places.name: Angkringan Lik Man
places.note: Where the charcoal-coffee trick was invented; still the definitive place to try it.

places.name: Angkringan carts on Jalan Wongsodirjan
places.note: Neighbouring carts serve the same thing with less of a queue.

places.name: Angkringan at Alun-Alun Kidul
places.note: Charcoal coffee and hot ginger drinks alongside the snack skewers.

landmarks: Borobudur Temple
The world's largest Buddhist temple, this 9th-century stepped pyramid of stone stupas is famed for its breathtaking sunrise views over volcanic mist.
Prambanan Temple
Indonesia's tallest Hindu temple complex, its soaring spires dedicated to Shiva, Vishnu, and Brahma make it a UNESCO World Heritage masterpiece.
Kraton Yogyakarta (Sultan's Palace)
The living royal palace of the Sultan of Yogyakarta preserves centuries of Javanese court culture, architecture, and traditional gamelan performances.
Taman Sari Water Castle
This atmospheric 18th-century royal bathing complex of pools, underground tunnels, and ruins offers a photogenic glimpse into sultanate-era leisure.
Malioboro Street
Yogyakarta's vibrant main thoroughfare buzzes with street vendors, batik shops, and horse-drawn carriages, making it the city's shopping and cultural pulse.
Mount Merapi
One of Indonesia's most active volcanoes looms over the city, drawing adventurers for sunrise jeep tours across its dramatic eruption-scarred slopes.
Parangtritis Beach
A wild, black-sand beach on the Indian Ocean famed for its towering dunes, horse-cart rides, and legends of the Queen of the Southern Sea.
Tugu Yogyakarta
This iconic white obelisk monument marks the symbolic axis of the city and stands as a beloved nighttime photo landmark for visitors.
Ratu Boko
Perched on a hilltop overlooking Prambanan, these mysterious palace ruins offer sweeping sunset vistas and an air of ancient royal mystery.
Alun-Alun Kidul
This lively southern square is famous for its twin sacred banyan trees and nighttime rentals of glowing pedal-powered light-up cars.

train.note: No international trains. Yogyakarta is one of the best-connected stops on Java's rail network, with Tugu station right in the middle of town on Jalan Malioboro and Lempuyangan handling economy services. Trains reach Jakarta in 7-8 hours, Surabaya in 4-5 and Bandung in about 7, and the daytime runs through the volcanic interior are genuinely scenic. Book on the KAI Access app from 45 days out.

bus.note: No international coaches. Giwangan is the main terminal, south-east of the centre, with Rosalia Indah, Sinar Jaya and Safari Dharma Raya running to Jakarta, Surabaya, Malang and Bali (about 16 hours including the Ketapang-Gilimanuk ferry). Book through redBus Indonesia (https://www.redbus.id/). For Borobudur and Prambanan, use the Trans Jogja city buses or a shuttle rather than an intercity coach.

ferry.note: Yogyakarta is inland with no port. The south-coast beaches at Parangtritis face the open Indian Ocean with dangerous surf and no passenger service. The nearest working ferry terminals are on the north coast at Semarang, about three hours away, with Pelni sailings to Kalimantan.

half.name: Kaliurang
half.blurb: Cool hillside resort town on the slopes of Mount Merapi with forest trails and volcano viewpoints.

half.name: Goa Pindul
half.blurb: Limestone cave in the Gunung Kidul hills where visitors float through on inner tubes past stalactites.

half.name: Kalibiru
half.blurb: Hilltop pine forest park with wooden viewing platforms overlooking a reservoir and the hills below.

full.name: Dieng Plateau
full.blurb: High volcanic plateau with ancient Hindu temple ruins, sulfurous craters, and a colored crater lake.
